title: Line Walk: Five Kinds of Lines
students: Trace dotted straight, curvy, zigzag, wavy and spiral lines with a finger, then crayon, then draw each one again on your own.

title: Line Hunt on the Playground
students: Circle and mark: find 3 zigzag, 3 curvy and 3 straight lines in a playground line drawing, using a different crayon for each kind.

title: Shape Shadows Match
students: Cut and glue: cut out a circle, square, triangle and rectangle and glue each onto its matching shadow outline.

title: Build a Robot from Shapes
students: Cut and glue collage: build a robot from paper circles, squares, rectangles and triangles, then tally how many of each shape you used.

title: Red, Yellow, Blue: First Colors
students: Draw it: in three boxes the teacher reads aloud, draw one thing that is red, one yellow and one blue, then trace each color word.

title: Color Mixing Surprise
students: Predict by circling what red and yellow make, mix them with paint or crayon, then color the result box and mark if you were right.

title: Color by Mix: Garden Picture
students: Color by code: each space shows two primary dots, so color it the secondary color they make, finishing a garden with orange, green and purple.

title: Calm Lines, Jumpy Lines
students: Cut and sort: sort 6 line cards into calm and jumpy boxes, then draw one calm line and one jumpy line of your own.

title: My Shape Picture Plan
students: Choose a house, animal or car to make, circle the shapes you will need from a shape bank, then sketch it in the frame.

title: Lines, Shapes and Colors Check
students: Circle the zigzag line, the triangle and the mixed color in 6 picture rows the teacher reads aloud.

title: What Do You See? The Great Wave
students: Look at Hokusai's The Great Wave, circle a boat, a mountain and the foam, then draw the part you like best.

title: Starry Night Swirl Search
students: Trace the swirly lines on a black-and-white copy of Van Gogh's The Starry Night, then finish the drawing with your own swirly sky.

title: Stripe Patterns from Ghana
students: Finish the pattern: look at a kente cloth photo, then continue 3 stripe patterns by drawing the next shapes and colors.

title: Paper Cutting from China
students: Fold and cut along a dotted line to make a symmetrical paper-cut flower like Chinese jianzhi, then glue it in the frame.

title: Mola Layers from Panama
students: Cut and glue collage: after seeing a Guna mola photo, layer three colors of paper shapes to make a mola-style animal.

title: Two Animal Artworks
students: Same or different: compare Dürer's Young Hare and an Egyptian cat statue by circling picture clues in a two-column chart.

title: What Is It Made Of?
students: Cut and sort: glue 6 artwork pictures under clay, cloth, paper or paint, then draw one more artwork made of clay.

title: Art Around the World Map
students: Match: draw a line from 4 artworks to the place on a simple world map where each was made.

title: I Like This Art Because
students: Pick a favorite from 4 small artworks, draw it, and finish the read-aloud frame "I like it because I see ___."

title: Art Around the World Check
students: Match 5 artworks to their materials and circle the one with a repeating pattern.

title: Pick a Happy Moment
students: Circle a picture choice for a happy moment (a game, a snow day, a picnic), then sketch the main thing in a big box.

title: Drawing Me with Shapes
students: Draw and label: build a self-portrait from a circle head and rectangle body, then add arms and legs doing a favorite action.

title: Big Me, Small Background
students: Draw yourself big in the front box and a park, beach or classroom small in the back box, then put them together.

title: Add the Weather
students: Finish the drawing: add sun, rain or snow to 3 plain scenes with lines and colors, then draw your own weather day.

title: Feelings Faces
students: Finish the drawing: add line eyes and mouths to 4 blank faces to show happy, sad, surprised and sleepy, then pick one for your story.

title: First and Last Picture Story
students: Draw what happened first and what happened last in two boxes about a fun day at school.

title: Snack Time Still Life
students: Draw a favorite fruit or snack from shapes, then add lines to show if it is bumpy, smooth or crunchy.

title: Why These Colors?
students: Color your story picture, then circle why you picked the colors: real colors, favorite colors, or to show a feeling.

title: Tell Me About Your Art
students: Point and tell a partner about your picture, then color stars for the part you are proudest of.

title: Art About Me Check
students: Circle the picture that tells a story, the self-portrait and the background in 5 picture rows.

title: What Is a Museum?
students: Short read-aloud passage about a museum visit, then circle pictures of 4 things you would see there.

title: Museum Helpers Match
students: Match: draw lines from a guard, a guide and an art hanger to pictures of what each one does.

title: Pick One to Show
students: Look at 3 of your artworks, put a star on the one to show, and circle why: neat, finished or tells a story.

title: Frame It Up
students: Cut out a paper frame, decorate it with a repeating line pattern, and glue a small drawing inside.

title: My Art Label
students: Museum label: trace your first name and draw or dictate a title on a label card for your artwork.

title: Hang It Straight
students: Circle and mark: X the crooked pictures on a gallery wall drawing and draw arrows to show how to straighten them.

title: Gallery Walk Manners
students: Cut and sort: sort 6 pictures of museum behavior into yes and not yet boxes.

title: I Noticed Your Art
students: On a class gallery walk, draw a classmate's artwork and circle a smile for what you liked: color, lines or shapes.

title: Our Class Art Show Wall
students: Cut and glue: arrange 4 small artwork cards on a wall drawing so they are spaced out and easy to see.

title: Kindergarten Art Year Review
students: Circle and match across 8 picture rows: lines, shapes, colors, art from another place and a museum helper.

title: Line Zoo
students: Draw 6 animals using one line type each (thick, thin, dotted, spiral, zigzag, wavy), then write the line name under each.

title: Lines That Move
students: Finish the drawing: add action lines to 4 pictures (running dog, falling leaf, bouncing ball, windy flag) to show how they move.

title: Geometric or Organic?
students: Cut and sort: glue 10 shapes under geometric or organic, then draw one more of each that you find in the classroom.

title: Shape Animal Collage
students: Cut and glue collage: tear organic shapes and cut geometric shapes from scrap paper to build an animal, then circle which kind you used most.

title: Secondary Color Recipes
students: Fill in the blank: color the two primaries that make orange, green and violet on 3 recipe cards, then test each with crayons.

title: Six-Color Wheel Puzzle
students: Cut and glue 6 color wedges onto a wheel so each secondary color sits between the two primaries that make it.

title: Pattern Strips
students: Finish the pattern: continue 4 AB and ABC strips made of lines, shapes and colors, then design one strip of your own.

title: Shape Count Mystery Picture
students: Color by code: color triangles, circles and squares by a key to reveal a hidden picture, then count each shape.

title: Under the Sea Plan
students: Plan an underwater picture: circle 3 shapes, 3 line types and 2 secondary colors from banks, then sketch it.

title: Lines, Shapes and Colors Quick Check
students: Name 4 line types, sort 4 shapes as geometric or organic, and fill in 3 color recipes.

title: Rain in a Japanese Print
students: Look at Hiroshige's Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge, trace the rain lines, and circle how the people on the bridge feel.

title: Rangoli Halves from India
students: Symmetry half: finish a rangoli-style design on dot paper by copying each shape to the other side.

title: Papel Picado Banner
students: Fold and cut a papel picado flag along dotted guide lines after looking at photos of Mexican celebration banners.

title: Shapes in a Navajo Blanket
students: Find triangles, diamonds and stripes in a historic Navajo blanket photo, then continue its pattern on a square grid.

title: For Using or For Looking?
students: Cut and sort: sort 6 artworks into made for using or made for looking, then draw a pot with a pattern.

title: Animal Art Around the World
students: Compare a Chinese jade horse, Rousseau's Surprised! tiger and an Egyptian cat in a 3-column picture chart: what, where, made of.

title: Read a Museum Label
students: Circle the artist, title, place and material on a big museum label for Hokusai's Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji).

title: Art Passport Stamps
students: Draw a tiny copy of 4 artworks into passport stamp boxes and trace the place each one comes from.

title: I See, I Think, I Wonder
students: Pick one of 3 artworks and finish "I see", "I think" and "I wonder" frames with words or drawings.

title: Many Places Check
students: Match 5 artworks to where they come from and what they were for, then circle one pattern.

title: First, Next, Last Story Plan
students: Plan a 3-box picture story about a fun day (park, snow, a game) with a sketch and one word in each box.

title: Same Character, Three Places
students: Draw the same character in a kitchen, at a beach and on a snowy hill, then circle the place that fits your story.

title: Show the Action
students: Trace 4 stick-figure poses (running, jumping, reaching, sitting), then turn one into the main person in your story.

title: Close Up or Far Away?
students: Draw your story's main moment twice, once close up and once far away, then circle which shows feelings better.

title: Happy Day, Gloomy Day
students: Color the same scene twice, with bright colors for a happy day and dark colors for a gloomy day.

title: Details Make It Tell More
students: Finish the drawing: add 5 details (clothing pattern, weather, a pet, a toy, a sign) to a plain picture.

title: Choice Cards
students: Cut and glue: glue color, line, place and size cards next to sentences about choices you made in your picture.

title: Before and After: Fix One Thing
students: Circle one part of your story draft to add or change, then draw the improved part in the after box.

title: My Picture Tells
students: Fill in the blank: "My picture shows ___. I used ___ to show ___." with a picture word bank.

title: Art About My Life Check
students: Put 3 picture story boxes in order, circle the background, and name one artist choice.

title: Who Works at a Museum?
students: Match: connect 5 museum workers (curator, guard, guide, framer, artist) to job pictures, then draw one at work.

title: Choosing for a Show
students: Give 4 of your artworks 1 to 3 stars for neat, finished and tells a story, then pick one to show.

title: Museum Label Maker
students: Museum label writing: fill in artist name, title, materials and year on a label after a model label.

title: Mount It on a Mat
students: Glue a drawing centered on a bigger paper mat, checking equal borders with a cut paper measuring strip.

title: Handle with Care
students: Circle and mark: circle safe and X unsafe ways to carry, stack and store art in 8 pictures.

title: Gallery Wall Plan
students: Cut and glue: arrange 6 small artwork cards on a wall grid evenly spaced at eye level.

title: Docent for a Day
students: Plan a talk about one artwork: "This is ___. Look at ___. I like ___."

title: Visitor Comment Card
students: Visit a classmate's art and fill in a comment card with one thing you notice and one kind question.

title: Museum Walk Sketch Hunt
students: On a class museum walk, sketch 6 finds: a sculpture, a portrait, a landscape, a label, a frame and a pattern.

title: Grade 1 Art Year Review
students: Mixed review in 10 picture items: lines, shapes, color recipes, art from many places and museum jobs.

title: Texture Rubbing Collection
students: Make 6 crayon rubbings of classroom textures, label each rough, bumpy, smooth or ridged, then match each to a drawn texture.

title: Draw the Feel
students: Draw fur, bark, brick, scales and feathers in 5 boxes using lines and dots after an example box.

title: Shape to Form
students: Draw and label: turn a circle, square and triangle into a sphere, cube and cone by following step drawings.

title: Light to Dark Value Steps
students: Fill a 5-step value strip by pressing harder with a pencil, then shade a ball from light to dark.

title: Mixing Chart
students: Predict, mix and paint a 3-by-3 chart of primary pairs, then circle any results that surprised you.

title: Mirror Bugs
students: Symmetry half: finish 4 half-drawn bugs and butterflies so both sides match, then design your own symmetrical creature.

title: Elements Hunt in a Jungle
students: Draw and label: find a line, shape, form, texture and color in Rousseau's Surprised! and label each on the copy.

title: Positive and Negative Shapes
students: Cut a shape from the middle of a paper square and glue both parts side by side to show positive and negative space.

title: Textured Creature Plan
students: Plan an imaginary creature: choose its line, shape, texture and color from banks, then sketch it.

title: Elements of Art Check
students: Name line, shape, form, texture, value and color in 8 small pictures and write 2 color recipes.

title: Two Waves Compared
students: Venn diagram: compare Hokusai's The Great Wave and Winslow Homer's The Gulf Stream by colors, lines and feelings.

title: Pysanky Egg Design
students: Finish the drawing: design a Ukrainian pysanka-style egg outline using bands, symbols and line patterns from traditional examples.

title: Adinkra Symbol Cloth
students: Learn 4 adinkra symbols from Ghana and their meanings, then draw a stamped-cloth grid repeating the one you choose.

title: Story on a Greek Vase
students: Describe the scene on a Greek black-figure vase, then draw what happens next on a blank vase outline.

title: Roman Mosaic Animal
students: Cut and glue paper squares into a small mosaic animal after looking at a Roman floor mosaic.

title: Festival Art
students: Match 4 festival artworks (Chinese lantern, Japanese carp streamer, Guatemalan giant kite, Indian diya lamp) to their celebrations, then design one.

title: Who Made the Lanterns?
students: Short passage (60 words) about lantern makers, then answer 3 questions and circle the sentence that tells the material.

title: Why Did They Make It?
students: Cut and sort: sort 6 artworks by purpose (to use, to tell a story, to remember, to celebrate) and write one reason each.

title: My Opinion with Reasons
students: Choose one of 3 artworks and write 2 sentences: "I like (or do not like) it because..." using an art word.

title: Many Places Review
students: Match artworks to cultures, purposes and materials, then explain one comparison in a sentence.

title: Moment Brainstorm
students: List or sketch 4 everyday moments worth drawing (a game, a walk, a meal, the weather), then star the best story.

title: Three Thumbnails
students: Draw the same moment as 3 small thumbnails from different viewpoints, then pick one to enlarge.

title: Near and Far
students: Divide a scene into foreground and background, drawing near things big and low and far things small and high.

title: How Do They Feel?
students: Draw 4 characters showing feelings with face and body, then write the feeling word under each.

title: Four-Panel Comic Story
students: Tell a story in 4 comic panels with one speech bubble each about a pretend or real fun moment.

title: Choosing Materials
students: Compare crayon, marker, colored pencil and collage for your story in a chart (bright, detailed, easy), then choose.

title: Halfway Check-In
students: Check off what is done, write one problem you had and how you will fix it.

title: Two Stars and a Wish
students: Give a partner's story picture two stars and a wish using art words from a word bank.

title: Artist Statement Frame
students: Write 3 sentences about your story picture: what happens, one choice you made, and why.

title: Art About My Life Review
students: Order story steps, name foreground and background, and match choices to reasons in 6 items.

title: A Museum's Big Jobs
students: Short passage (80 words) on how museums collect, protect and show art, then answer 4 questions.

title: Curator's Choice
students: Cut and sort: group 9 small artworks into 3 shows by theme (animals, weather, people) and name each show.

title: Choose and Explain
students: Pick 2 of your artworks for a class show and write why each was chosen.

title: Getting Art Ready
students: Cut and glue 6 steps for preparing art (finish, sign, mount, label, hang, check) in order, then draw the finished piece.

title: Hallway Show Map
students: Draw and label a floor plan of the hallway show marking 8 artworks, a welcome sign and labels.

title: Welcome Sign Design
students: Design a show welcome sign with a title in big block letters and a border pattern.

title: Tour Guide Script
students: Write a 4-line tour script about one artwork for visitors.

title: Visitor Favorites Graph
students: Tally visitor votes for 5 artworks, make a picture graph, then answer 3 questions about it.

title: Judge the Display
students: Rate the class show on 4 criteria (neat, spaced, labeled, easy to see) and suggest one fix.

title: Grade 2 Art Year Review
students: Mixed review of elements, art from many places, story pictures and showing art in 10 items.

title: Build a 12-Color Wheel
students: Draw and label: color a 12-part wheel and label each primary, secondary and tertiary color in its place.

title: Tertiary Color Recipes
students: Fill in the blank: write and test 6 tertiary recipes (primary plus neighbor secondary), naming each like red-orange.

title: Warm and Cool Sort
students: Cut and sort 12 color chips into warm and cool, then draw a warm sun and a cool ocean using only those chips' colors.

title: Tint Ladder
students: Make a 5-step tint ladder from one color by adding white a little at a time, labeling each step.

title: Warm Night, Cool Night
students: Compare warm and cool color in Van Gogh's Café Terrace at Night and Picasso's The Old Guitarist, then name each mood.

title: Warm and Cool Mystery Picture
students: Color by code: spaces marked W get a warm color and C a cool one, revealing a sunset over water.

title: Bird Color Plan
students: Choose warm, cool or tints for a bird drawing, swatch your colors in boxes, then sketch the bird.

title: Color Theory Check
students: Fill in a blank wheel, name 4 tertiaries, sort warm and cool, and circle the tint ladder.

title: Overlap Makes Space
students: Redraw 3 rows of shapes so they overlap, then circle which shape looks closest in each row.

title: Big Near, Small Far
students: Finish the drawing: add 5 trees along a path, each smaller than the last as the path goes back.

title: Find the Horizon Line
students: Trace the horizon line in 4 landscape pictures and label the sky and ground in each.

title: Low Is Near, High Is Far
students: Cut and glue 6 houses onto a landscape so the lower ones look closer and the higher ones farther.

title: Space in Hunters in the Snow
students: Spot the design choice: find and label 3 examples of overlap, size and placement in Bruegel's The Hunters in the Snow.

title: Space Words Drawn
students: Draw a tiny picture for overlap, horizon line, foreground and background with one sentence each.

title: Landscape with Depth Plan
students: Plan a landscape with a horizon line, 3 overlapping hills and big-to-small objects, then check off each trick.

title: Space Tricks Check
students: Circle the space trick in 6 pictures and fix one flat drawing by adding overlap.

title: Cave Art: The First Pictures
students: Look at a Lascaux cave painting photo and answer 4 questions about the animals, the tools used and why it was made.

title: Draw It the Egyptian Way
students: Follow a step guide to draw a figure Egyptian style: side head, front eye, front chest, side legs.

title: Meet Vincent van Gogh
students: Short passage (150 words) about Van Gogh, answer 4 questions, then draw a small sky in his swirly style.

title: Monet's Haystacks All Day
students: Compare two of Monet's Haystacks at different times of day and describe how the light and colors change.

title: Hokusai's Mount Fuji
students: Find Mount Fuji in 3 of Hokusai's Thirty-Six Views and describe how he made it big or small each time.

title: Who Painted It?
students: Match 6 small artworks to Van Gogh, Monet, Hokusai or cave art using clue words like swirly, dotted or outlined.

title: From Cave to Canvas
students: Cut and glue 6 artworks in time order from cave art to Impressionism and write one clue about each.

title: Artists Check
students: Name artists from style clues, order 4 artworks in time and write one fact about each artist.

title: Handle with Care Rules
students: Cut and sort 10 actions (clean hands, carry flat, stack wet paintings) into safe and harmful for artwork.

title: Where Could Our Show Go?
students: Compare 3 real venues (library, school office, community center) for light, space and visitors, then choose one.

title: Pick Your Best Work
students: Rate 3 of your artworks with a 4-item checklist and choose one for the show with a reason.

title: Labels That Tell
students: Museum label writing: write 2 labels with artist, title, year, materials and one sentence about the work.

title: Protect the Art Task Cards
students: Task card strips: solve 4 display problems (sunny window, busy hallway, wet glue, tape tears) with a protection choice for each.

title: Exhibit Wall Sketch
students: Draw and label the venue wall, placing 8 artworks with even spacing and labels at the right height.

title: Visitor Response Cards
students: Design a visitor card asking for one observation and one question, then use it on a classmate's work.

title: After the Show
students: Answer 4 questions about what worked, what visitors noticed and what to change next time.

title: School Places Sketch Walk
students: Sketch 4 school places (playground, library, hallway, lunchroom) in quick 2-minute drawings with one mood word each.

title: Colors and Moods Match
students: Match 6 color sets to moods (calm, scary, cheerful, lonely), then explain one choice in a sentence.

title: Same Place, New Mood
students: Draw the playground twice, once cheerful and once spooky, changing only colors and weather.

title: Mood in Van Gogh's Bedroom
students: Answer: what place, what mood, and which colors and lines make it, for Van Gogh's The Bedroom.

title: Mood Plan
students: Choose a school place and a mood, list the colors, lines and weather you will use, then sketch 2 thumbnails.

title: One Change Better
students: Compare your first draft to your plan and list 2 revisions that will make the mood stronger.

title: Mood Artist Statement
students: Write 4 sentences about your place, mood, art choices and one revision you made.

title: Grade 3 Art Year Review
students: Mixed review of the color wheel, space tricks, artists, exhibits and mood in 12 items.

title: Tint, Hue, Shade Scale
students: Make a 7-step scale from tint to pure hue to shade by adding white or black, labeling each step.

title: Complement Clue Puzzle
students: Crossword with real clues: use a color wheel to solve 8 clues like "my complement is violet" and fill in the grid.

title: Analogous Color Fans
students: Fan out 3 sets of analogous colors from the wheel, then paint a leaf using one set.

title: One-Color Landscape
students: Paint a small landscape using only tints and shades of one hue, naming the hue and steps used.

title: Complements in The Night Café
students: Find the red and green complements in Van Gogh's The Night Café and describe the mood they create.

title: Color Scheme Detective
students: Label 6 small artworks as monochromatic, analogous or complementary and give one clue each.

title: Still Life Color Plan
students: Choose a color scheme for a still life, swatch tints and shades, and justify the mood in 2 sentences.

title: Color Schemes Check
students: Identify schemes, finish a tint and shade scale, and name 4 complementary pairs.

title: Foreground, Middle Ground, Background
students: Draw and label the three grounds in 3 landscapes and add one object to each ground.

title: Atmospheric Hills
students: Paint 4 rows of hills, each farther row lighter, bluer and less detailed.

title: Detail Fades Away
students: Draw the same flower near, middle and far, showing less detail each time.

title: Where Is Eye Level?
students: Draw a box above, on and below a horizon line and write which sides of each box you can see.

title: Depth in The Oxbow
students: Spot the design choice: label 4 depth tricks and the three grounds in Thomas Cole's The Oxbow.

title: Space Fixer Task Cards
students: Task card strips: fix 4 flat drawings by adding overlap, size change, placement or atmospheric color, naming each fix.

title: Deep Landscape Plan
students: Plan a landscape with all three grounds and 4 depth tricks, checking a list before drawing.

title: Space and Depth Check
students: Identify depth tricks in 6 pictures and draw a three-ground scene in a small frame.

title: Leonardo's Notebook Page
students: Study a Leonardo da Vinci notebook page and answer 4 questions about what he observed and drew.

title: Impressionist Brushstrokes
students: Paint a small scene with quick, broken dabs of color like the Impressionists, following a model.

title: Pointillism Dots
students: Place dots of two primaries side by side to make secondary colors, then fill a fruit drawing with dots.

title: Seurat's Sunday Afternoon
students: Describe how dots, shapes and space make Seurat's A Sunday on La Grande Jatte feel calm and still.

title: Monet or Van Gogh?
students: T-chart: compare Impressionism and Post-Impressionism through Monet and Van Gogh by brushwork, color, subject and feeling.

title: Van Gogh Copies Hiroshige
students: Compare Hiroshige's Plum Park in Kameido with Van Gogh's copy and list 4 things he borrowed.

title: Renaissance to 1900
students: Place 6 artworks on a timeline from 1500 to 1900 with the movement name and a style clue.

title: Artist Trading Card
students: Make a trading card for a chosen artist with dates, movement, a famous work and 3 style facts.

title: Venue Scout Report
students: Study a real venue (library, town hall), record wall space, light and visitor traffic, and rate it.

title: Measure a Mat
students: Measure 3 artworks and work out mat sizes so each piece has an equal 2-inch border.

title: Condition Check
students: Inspect 3 artworks and fill in a condition chart for tears, smudges, bent corners and loose parts.

title: Artist Statement Draft
students: Draft a 5-sentence artist statement about one exhibited piece with a frame for each sentence.

title: Exhibit Floor Plan
students: Draw and label a floor plan on grid paper showing walls, artworks, labels and a visitor path.

title: Show Poster and Invitation
students: Design a show poster and invitation with title, date, place and one featured image.

title: Show Day Job Chart
students: Assign jobs (greeter, docent, setup, cleanup) with tasks and checklists for the class exhibit.

title: Did the Exhibit Work?
students: Evaluate the exhibit with a 5-criteria rubric and write 2 suggestions.

title: Viewfinder Sketches
students: Cut a paper viewfinder and sketch 3 framings of one place near school.

title: Viewpoint Changes Mood
students: Draw the same street from bird's-eye, eye-level and worm's-eye views and describe the mood of each.

title: Morning, Noon, Night
students: Shade one building three times with value and color to show different times and moods.

title: Two Landscapes, Two Moods
students: Compare Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog and Monet's Impression, Sunrise for place, mood and choices.

title: Mood Board
students: Cut and glue sketches, color swatches and words into a mood board for your chosen place and feeling.

title: Is the Mood Clear?
students: Guess a classmate's intended mood from their draft, then give 2 specific suggestions with art words.

title: Revision Record
students: Record 3 revisions, why each was made and how each changed the mood.

title: Grade 4 Art Year Review
students: Mixed review of color schemes, depth, movements, exhibiting and mood in 12 items.

title: Triads and Split Complements
students: Draw triangles and Y-shapes on a 12-part wheel to mark triadic and split-complementary schemes, then swatch each.

title: Bright to Dull
students: Lower a hue's intensity in 5 steps by mixing in its complement, making a neutral scale.

title: Mixing Browns and Grays
students: Mix 6 neutrals from complement pairs, record recipes, and match 3 to natural objects like bark or stone.

title: What Colors Mean
students: Short passage (200 words) on what red, white and green mean in 4 cultures, then answer questions on meaning and context.

title: Wild Color: Fauvism
students: Explain how unnatural color shows feeling in Matisse's The Open Window, Collioure.

title: One Poster, Three Schemes
students: Color the same poster design in 3 schemes and predict how each changes the message.

title: Expressive Color Proposal
students: Choose a scheme for an expressive still life, test swatches and justify it in 3 sentences.

title: Advanced Color Check
students: Identify 6 schemes, finish intensity steps and explain one symbolic color choice.

title: Roads, Rails and Fences
students: Draw a road, a railroad and a fence that all narrow to one point on the horizon.

title: Spot the Vanishing Point
students: Extend edge lines in 4 paintings and photos to find each vanishing point and horizon.

title: Lampposts in a Row
students: Use guide lines to draw a row of lampposts and trees shrinking toward a vanishing point.

title: The Avenue at Middelharnis
students: Trace converging lines in Hobbema's painting and explain how the road pulls your eye in.

title: Pointing at You
students: Draw a pencil, a book and a shoe pointing toward you next to side views to practice foreshortening.

title: All the Depth Tricks
students: Draw a landscape using overlap, size, placement, atmospheric perspective and converging lines, checking each off.

title: Space Words in Action
students: Word map: define and sketch 6 terms (vanishing point, converging lines, foreshortening and more) and use each about an artwork.

title: Space Check
students: Find vanishing points, name depth tricks and correct 2 drawing errors.

title: Many Views at Once
students: Draw a cup from 3 angles, then combine pieces into one Cubist-style drawing after Picasso and Braque.

title: Kandinsky and Music
students: Describe the lines, shapes and colors in Kandinsky's Composition VII and what music they suggest.

title: Feelings First: The Scream
students: Explain how color and line in Munch's The Scream make it expressionist.

title: Exhibit Design and Flow
students: Draw and label a gallery layout with sightlines, visitor path, lighting and accessibility notes.

title: Catalog Essay Draft
students: Draft a 300-word catalog essay introducing your curated show.

title: Loans and Conservation
students: Short passage on loan agreements and conservation needs, then answer 4 scenario questions.

title: Investigation Peer Review
students: Review a peer's investigation with a rubric for inquiry, practice and synthesis.

title: Midyear Portfolio Reflection
students: Evaluate progress on your investigation and set next steps.

title: Contemporary Issue Research
students: Analyze 3 sources on a present-day issue for claims, data and images.

title: Tradition and Innovation
students: Short passage on artists reinventing traditions (Hokusai and Western perspective, Van Gogh and ukiyo-e), then answer questions.

title: Visual Research Board
students: Cut and glue sketches of 8 historical references onto a research board with notes.

title: Controlled Experiment Series
students: Run 5 material experiments changing one variable each and record results.

title: Nine Concept Thumbnails
students: Develop 9 thumbnails combining issue and tradition, then select 2 with reasons.

title: Representing Others Respectfully
students: Short passage on representing communities respectfully, then apply its guidelines to 4 scenarios.

title: Six-Week Production Timeline
students: Build a production timeline with milestones and critique checkpoints.

title: Studio Documentation Log
students: Document each studio session with sketches, decisions and problems.

title: Artist Talk Outline
students: Outline a 3-minute talk on issue, tradition, process and outcome.

title: Grade 11 Art Year Review
students: Mixed review of critical lenses, three-point and composition, curation and investigation in 12 items.

title: What Is Art?
students: Short passage (650 words) on mimetic, expressive, formal and institutional theories, then test each on Duchamp's Fountain (1917).

title: Exhibition Review
students: Write a 400-word review of a mini exhibition of 6 public-domain works with claims and evidence.

title: Juror's Statement
students: Jury 8 sample artworks with weighted criteria and write a juror's statement explaining the awards.

title: Ensō and Black Square
students: Compare a Hakuin ensō and Malevich's Black Square and discuss how culture shapes interpretation.

title: The 1913 Armory Show
students: Analyze press reactions to Duchamp's Nude Descending a Staircase and the criteria critics used.

title: Van Gogh's Reputation
students: Build a timeline of Van Gogh's reputation from 1890 to today with 6 events and their causes.

title: Artists Against the Eiffel Tower
students: Evaluate the 1887 artists' protest letter against the Eiffel Tower and how judgments of public art change.

title: Critiquing Your Own Best Work
students: Write a critical analysis of your own strongest piece using the full critique process.

title: Sharpen a Critique
students: Revise a sample critique for precision, evidence and vocabulary with marked changes.

title: Critique Capstone Check
students: Write a timed critique of an unseen work using a chosen lens and aesthetic theory.

title: Cézanne's Tilted Tables
students: Analyze how Cézanne mixes viewpoints in Still Life with Basket and why it matters for modern art.

title: Curvilinear Perspective
students: Draw a fisheye-style street using a curved horizon and curved vertical guides.

title: Forced Perspective Illusion
students: Design a forced-perspective illusion like Borromini's gallery at Palazzo Spada and explain how it fools the eye.

title: Anamorphic Drawing
students: Grid for scaling: use a stretched grid to draw an image that looks correct only from one angle.

title: Other Ways to Show Space
students: Compare spatial systems in a Byzantine icon, a Chinese handscroll and a Persian miniature.

title: Composition for Meaning
students: Plan a composition where perspective choices support a stated meaning, with 4 thumbnails and rationale.

title: Las Meninas Analysis
students: Overlay vanishing point, gaze lines and composition structure on Velázquez's Las Meninas.

title: Sustained Drawing Log
students: Log a 4-week sustained drawing with goals, hours and critiques.

title: Spatial Problem Set
students: Solve 5 construction problems: diagonals, shadows, inclined planes, circles and reflections.

title: Space and Composition Capstone Check
students: Complete a complex perspective task and justify your composition choices.

title: Portfolios for Different Audiences
students: Compare what art school, college admissions, jobs and competitions look for in a chart.

title: Twenty Down to Twelve
students: Edit 20 works down to 12 with a partner, recording criteria and reasons for each cut.

title: Senior Show Logistics
students: Plan venue, schedule, budget, install crew and publicity for a senior exhibition.

title: Wall Text and Catalog Entries
students: Write the show's introductory wall text and catalog entries for 2 of your works.

title: Installation Diagram
students: Draw and label a final installation with measurements, 57-inch center hanging height and lighting.

title: Copyright for Artists
students: Short passage on copyright, public domain and fair use, then decide on 6 scenarios.

title: Opening Night Run of Show
students: Plan an opening with roles, a timed run of show and accessibility needs.

title: Show Feedback Data
students: Tally comment cards and attendance counts into a chart and judge what worked.

title: Portfolio Defense Prep
students: Prepare answers to 6 review questions about intent, growth and process.

title: Final Portfolio Reflection
students: Reflect on growth across your portfolio using 3 pieces as evidence.

title: Capstone Proposal
students: Propose a capstone linking a present-day issue to a historical tradition with research plan and timeline.

title: Annotated Bibliography
students: Annotate 5 historical and current sources for relevance to your capstone.

title: Tradition Lineage Map
students: Trace your tradition through 6 key works to today on a timeline with notes on change.

title: Artists Respond to Their Time
students: Short passage on Goya's The Third of May 1808 and Käthe Kollwitz's prints, then answer how artists responded to events.

title: Prototype and Test
students: Build 3 studies, record viewer responses to each and decide a direction.

title: Capstone Panel Critique
students: Present your capstone in progress to a panel and record feedback as action items.

title: Process Book Spreads
students: Design 2 process book spreads showing research, experiments and decisions.

title: Capstone Statement
students: Write a 300-word statement connecting issue, tradition and your work.

title: Capstone Reflection
students: Evaluate the capstone against your proposal goals and describe what you learned.

title: Grade 12 Art Capstone Review
students: Mixed review of aesthetics, spatial systems, curation and investigation in 12 items.
